candidates.title: Microsoft MXC gives local coding agents a policy boundary across operating systems
candidates.summary: Microsoft made its open-source MXC containment SDK generally available as GitHub made MXC-backed local sandboxing generally available in Copilot CLI, the Copilot app, and VS Code Agent Host sessions.
candidates.what_changed: Agent builders can express filesystem, network, UI, process, and containment requirements through one versioned policy and typed SDKs, while Copilot now exposes a production integration across Windows, macOS, and Linux with enterprise enforcement controls.
candidates.why_it_matters: Local coding agents inherit powerful host authority. Moving policy outside the workload gives teams a reusable least-privilege boundary, but the documented security properties and enforcement gaps still vary by backend, operating system, and harness path.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: Treat an agent sandbox as executable security configuration: choose a backend from the threat model, test denied operations, identify in-process tools outside OS interception, and require fail-closed behavior when the host cannot enforce policy.

evidence.rationale: Microsoft documents the GA SDK, policy model, backends, and operating modes; GitHub documents a shipping Copilot integration and its limitations. Independent security testing was not located.
evidence.independent_validation: None verified. The implementation is publicly inspectable, but this run did not penetration-test it.
evidence.claim_scope: Availability and documented architecture are verified; comparative isolation strength and security outcomes are not independently validated.

signal.rationale: A cross-platform policy layer adopted by a major coding-agent product materially changes how teams can constrain local agent tool execution.

learning_gap.existing_explainer_status: Pulse has covered sandboxing incidents and product controls, but not a reusable comparison of process sandboxes, session isolation, containers, and microVMs.
learning_gap.suggested_explainer: Process Sandboxes, Containers, and MicroVMs for AI Agents

follow_up_opportunities.reason: Teams need a repeatable method for deriving, testing, and regression-checking least-privilege policies for coding-agent workloads.

deduplication.canonical_event: Microsoft MXC and its GitHub Copilot local-sandbox integration become generally available on October 7, 2026.
deduplication.material_delta: No prior Pulse story or merged ledger covers MXC or Copilot's MXC-backed local sandboxing.

publication_verification.notes: First-party architecture and integration details are consistent; no independent security evaluation was claimed.

candidates.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 cuts small-model prices and changes migration semantics
candidates.summary: Anthropic released Haiku 5.5 for high-volume work with lower tiered token prices, adjustable effort, browser and computer-use support, and a migration contract that changes token accounting, thinking, sampling, prefill, and tool behavior.
candidates.what_changed: The fixed `claude-haiku-5-5` model ID is available across Anthropic's supported platforms. Prompts at or below 100,000 tokens receive the lowest pricing tier, while the newer tokenizer and API semantics require integration changes beyond a model-name swap.
candidates.why_it_matters: The release makes small-model routing more economical for bounded subagent and high-volume tasks, but naive migration can produce request errors, changed budgets, truncated output, or invalid conversation replay.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: Migrate on a branch, apply the documented request changes, recount representative prompts, and compare complete successful-task cost at several effort levels before changing a production route.

evidence.rationale: Anthropic documents availability, exact prices, API changes, benchmark setup, and safety evaluation. Comparative performance remains vendor-reported, with launch testimonials selected by Anthropic.
evidence.independent_validation: Launch materials include first-hand customer evaluations, but this run found no independent public replication of the model's benchmark or production claims.
evidence.claim_scope: The story treats availability, prices, and integration contracts as verified; capability and average-cost claims remain scoped to Anthropic's measurements.

signal.rationale: A large price decrease plus adjustable effort and migration-breaking behavior can materially change production routing, cost models, and agent-loop integrations.

learning_gap.existing_explainer_status: The briefing directly explains the pricing tiers, effort control, and migration effects needed to act on the release.

deduplication.canonical_event: Anthropic releases Claude Haiku 5.5 on October 7, 2026.
deduplication.material_delta: Haiku 5.5 is a distinct model release with new price tiers and migration semantics; prior Pulse coverage concerns Sonnet 5.5.

publication_verification.notes: Availability, pricing, and migration requirements are verified from Anthropic sources; benchmark results were not independently reproduced.

watchlist.title: GitHub adds a purpose-built model for unstructured secret detection
watchlist.summary: GitHub upgraded existing AI-detected password alerts to a fine-tuned classifier that reads surrounding code and announced private-preview or forthcoming checks for push protection and Copilot security review.

evidence.rationale: GitHub documents the model's intended role, rollout stages, eligibility, and planned AI Credit billing, but publishes no detection-quality evaluation.

signal.rationale: Context-aware detection for credentials without recognizable token formats could materially affect pre-commit and push-time security workflows.

watchlist.reason: The installed alert scanner changed, but the most consequential push and Copilot workflows remain private preview or forthcoming, and GitHub did not publish precision, recall, or false-positive data.
promote_when: Public rollout with implementation and operating details.
Independent benchmark or GitHub-published detection-quality evaluation.

watchlist.title: Microsoft previews local MAI Code 1.1 Flash routing for GitHub Copilot
watchlist.summary: Microsoft described a quantized local coding model and future Copilot routing between on-device and cloud inference, with initial performance and benchmark results on new Surface hardware.

evidence.rationale: The technical write-up provides configuration and first-party results, but broad availability is forthcoming and measurements are limited to a vendor-selected hardware and software stack.

signal.rationale: Practical local-cloud routing in a mainstream coding agent could change latency, privacy, resilience, and workstation requirements.

watchlist.reason: The routing experience is described as coming soon, and the current performance evidence is a first-party evaluation on specific new hardware.
promote_when: Official release in Copilot with supported hardware and configuration details.
Independent latency, quality, memory, and power measurements.

exclusions.reason: GitHub Copilot availability is a distribution detail of the selected Claude Haiku 5.5 release, not a separate technical development.
Local-model discovery in Copilot CLI is incremental and belongs to the broader local-routing development retained on watch.
Updating a moving chat-latest pointer does not create a durable production API capability or stable model release.
Already retained on the October 7 watchlist; no new methodology, deployment evidence, or material delta was found.

editorial_opportunities.title: Process Sandboxes, Containers, and MicroVMs for AI Agents
editorial_opportunities.reason: MXC exposes a reusable distinction between policy portability and isolation strength that many engineers need before choosing an agent runtime boundary.

editorial_opportunities.title: Build and Test a Least-Privilege Policy for a Coding Agent
editorial_opportunities.reason: The release creates a practical need for an auditable workflow that maps tasks to grants, exercises denials, and regression-tests the boundary.
